mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the real discount rate applied to equities, thereby boosting the present value of future earnings and driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the FEDFUNDS trigger, or the 5-year real yield curve slope turns positive (indicating higher real rates).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to underperform in the following 60-day window due to market expectations of aggressive rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for three consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive or close to zero, or the 10-year real yield falls below the 2-year real yield (bond market signal of rate compression).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (labor market slack) creates a dual signal of full employment that anticipates a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the combined strength/weakness signal, or the correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE falls below 0.7 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (goods demand) of at least 5% for two consecutive months reduces future earnings growth expectations, producing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by >=5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or near zero, or GDP revisions indicate stronger than expected growth in the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in INDPRO (suppliers' production index) above 105 while HOUST (order book strength) remains below 1300 signals supply-side easing that precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 105 and HOUST remains below 1300 for three consecutive months
regime_hint: industrial production expanding but inventory levels still tight
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative, or the 10-day moving average of new orders turns down while production rises.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for two consecutive months in a period of rising FEDFUNDS, the combination of low labor market slack and higher policy rates is expected to suppress equity valuations, yielding a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS increasing
regime_hint: labor market loosening with higher policy rates
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the combined signal, or the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% in the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RSAFS (money demand) of at least 2% per month for three months indicates reduced liquidity pressures, which typically precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return in a normalization phase.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >=2% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the 7-day Treasury bill yield falls below 0.5% (indicating strong liquidity).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS (labor demand) and INDPRO (suppliers' production) above their 2021 Q4 averages for two months suggests a supply-demand balance that supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 145,000 and INDPRO > 104 for two consecutive months (2021 Q4 averages: PAYEMS 143, INDPRO 103)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative, or either PAYEMS or INDPRO reverts to below their respective reference levels before the return window.
